subject: physics
question_text: Show that for a projectile launched at an angle of 45°, the maximum height is one quarter of the range.

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), SHORT ANSWER **5 of Unit 4, two-star. ITS OWN FILE, NOT A CUT of the projectile question: a cut can only SELECT from steps that are already authored, and this answer needs new ones — substituting 45° into each result. It quotes H and R rather than deriving them, which is what the book does and what the question asks. SHIPS WITH ONE CUT: there is no 8-mark form of a substitution proof. The 1/1/1/1 split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The two results
lines: For a projectile thrown with speed u at
an angle θ, the standard results are
steps.margin_note: Quote both formulae before substituting. The examiner wants to see what you are starting from.
steps.why: This question does not ask you to derive anything. It asks you to put one value of θ into two results you already know, so writing them down correctly is most of the work.
common_mistakes: Writing sin θ instead of sin²θ in the height.
Writing sin θ instead of sin 2θ in the range.

recall.must_convey: That the two standard results H = u² sin²θ / 2g and R = u² sin 2θ / g are the starting point.
accept: start with the height and range formulas
H is u squared sin squared theta by two g
R is u squared sin two theta by g

write down the maximum height and range expressions
reject: put theta equals forty five degrees
so H is R by four

steps.label: Sketch (extra)
steps.margin_note: Not marked. This figure is drawn to scale — measure H and R on it and the ratio really is one to four.
steps.why: The answer is a ratio, so a picture drawn to scale lets you check it by eye before you trust the algebra. At 45° the path is much flatter than students expect.
common_mistakes: Sketching a tall narrow arch, which makes H look bigger than R/4 and hides the result.

recall.must_convey: That a sketch is drawn. Naming it is full credit.
accept: a small figure
draw the path at forty five degrees
sketch geestha
I draw the parabola with H and R marked
then the diagram

steps.label: Height at 45°
steps.margin_note: Show the sin²45° = 1/2 line. Jumping straight to u²/4g loses the working mark.
steps.why: Squaring 1/√2 to get 1/2 is the only real step here, and it is where the 4 in the final answer comes from.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to square, which gives u²/(2√2 g).

recall.must_convey: That substituting 45° into H gives u² / 4g.
accept: put forty five in the height formula
sin forty five squared is half
height becomes u squared by four g
H lo forty five pedatha
H equals u squared over four g
reject: range becomes u squared by g
so H is R by four

steps.label: Range at 45°
steps.margin_note: The angle inside the sine is 2θ, so it becomes 90°, not 45°.
steps.why: This is why 45° gives the greatest range: sin 2θ reaches its largest value, 1, exactly when 2θ is 90°.
common_mistakes: Writing sin 45° instead of sin 90° in the range.
Leaving the answer as u² sin 90° / g without evaluating it.

recall.must_convey: That substituting 45° into R gives u² / g, because sin 90° = 1.
accept: two theta becomes ninety degrees
sin ninety is one so range is u squared by g
put forty five in the range formula
R lo pedithe u square by g
range becomes u squared over g
reject: height becomes u squared by four g
so H is R by four

steps.label: Compare them
steps.margin_note: Say which numbered line you are substituting into. Box the final relation.
steps.why: Both results carry the same u²/g, so replacing it by R removes u and g together and leaves a pure ratio — which is what the question asked for.
common_mistakes: Stopping at H = u²/4g without bringing R back in.
Writing R = H/4, the ratio the wrong way round.

recall.must_convey: That u²/g is replaced by R to give H = R/4.
accept: substitute u squared by g equals R
so H is R by four
maximum height is one quarter of the range
